chunks: He asked him about a man who kills a mosquito, a flea, a louse, and a fly while he is in salat (prayer): does that invalidate his salat (prayer) and his wudu (ablution)?

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man being asked about in the legal case
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act being discussed
key_terms.الْبَقَّةَ: a mosquito or small biting insect killed during prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), whose validity is being questioned
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), whose validity is being questioned

ai.seo_question: Does killing a flea, louse, mosquito, or fly during salat invalidate the prayer or wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith states that killing small harmful insects during salat (prayer) does not invalidate either the salat (prayer) or the wudu (ablution). It conveys a concise legal ruling concerning minor actions occurring during worship.
